geometry.closure_rule: a vector is copied into region j when d_j <= d_1 * (1 + eps), for the four nearest regions
geometry.cap_note: Four is the copy cap of the spec's semantic_sharded reference configuration, not a property of the corpus. base.bin carries four distances because the model stores at most four copies.

boundary_crispness.definition: Fraction of base vectors whose second-nearest centroid distance exceeds 1.20 x their nearest centroid distance, under k-means with 256 centroids (seed 20260908, 20 iterations). Higher is crisper.

ambiguous_query_rate.definition: fraction of queries with d2 <= 1.10 * d1 against the same centroids

skew_top10_share.definition: share of base vectors in the 10 largest centroid regions

drift.definition: Centroids trained on records with update_date before 2019-01-01; recall@10 at one-region routing measured separately on queries whose source paper is before / after that date. Reported as the pair.

published.note: Published values are the cross-environment contract. A local build reproduces them within tolerance; it does not reproduce the bytes.

receipt.finding: Three builds, three environments: build 1 on the pod template's numpy 2.1.2 (RTX 4090), build 2 in an isolated venv honouring requirements.txt exactly (RTX 4090), build 3 in that same pinned environment on an RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell. All three produced byte-identical sampling receipts - sample.jsonl.zst 404cb92e... and query_ids.json a0f3236c... in every build - and three distinct vector digests, and so three distinct ground-truth, characterization and projection digests. Every published value agreed at the precision printed. The drift pair is the only value that moves at all: 0.523/0.549, 0.524/0.551, 0.522/0.549 across the three builds, a spread of 0.002 against a tolerance of 0.02. Artifact digests are environment-specific; reproducing the published values within tolerance, not the bytes, is the cross-environment claim this fixture makes.

findings.note: Boundary crispness 0.036 and ambiguous-query rate 0.891: under k-means with 256 centroids this embedding space has almost no crisp region boundaries. Distances concentrate, consistent with an intrinsic dimensionality of 32.55.

Semantic-sharded reaches recall@10 0.932 only at 3.715x storage, with the closure cap saturated (p50 copies = 4 of a maximum 4). Single-node HNSW reaches 0.997 at 1x. On this fixture the semantic-sharded family loses on both axes at once.

Drift pair 0.522 before / 0.549 after: routing post-2019 queries against centroids trained only on pre-2019 records carries no penalty on this fixture. The later queries score marginally higher, not lower.

Essentially all of the semantic-sharded loss is partitioning, not the index. recall@10 0.9320 against a routing ceiling of 0.9324 (characterization.json, build 3) leaves an index loss of 0.0004 - 8 of 20,000 neighbour slots. Both round to 0.932 at the precision published above, so the published pair is equal while the underlying measurement is not: the index loss is negligible, not zero.

Three builds, three environments: build 1 on the pod template's numpy 2.1.2 (RTX 4090), build 2 in an isolated venv honouring requirements.txt exactly (RTX 4090), build 3 in that same pinned environment on an RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell. All three produced byte-identical sampling receipts - sample.jsonl.zst 404cb92e... and query_ids.json a0f3236c... in every build - and three distinct vector digests, and so three distinct ground-truth, characterization and projection digests. Every published value agreed at the precision printed. The drift pair is the only value that moves at all: 0.523/0.549, 0.524/0.551, 0.522/0.549 across the three builds, a spread of 0.002 against a tolerance of 0.02. Artifact digests are environment-specific; reproducing the published values within tolerance, not the bytes, is the cross-environment claim this fixture makes.

Build 3's ground-view export recomputed the geometry from the artifacts the build had just written, independently of the characterization step, and reproduced every published value it could check: boundary crispness 0.0363 against 0.036, ambiguous query rate 0.8915 against 0.891, skew_top10_share 0.0754 against 0.075 - each within 0.0005 - and one-region recall@10 0.5473, inside the band implied by the drift pair. This is the first live value reproduction in the project: until now the fixture's own verification checked digests only.

Copies histogram at epsilon = 0.20: 1 copy 3.6%, 2 copies 5.6%, 3 copies 6.5%, 4 copies 84.3%. Closure replicates 84% of the corpus all the way to the cap of four regions, which is the mechanism behind the 3.715x storage amplification - not a long tail of awkward vectors but the common case.

family_line.note: The configuration task 012's brief asked for. decision_log_quoted.text: 8 configuration(s) were measured and judged against 5 constraint(s): recall_at_k, storage_amplification, latency_p95, qps, monthly_budget.

These options are indistinguishable on recall: hash_sharded[M=32,efSearch=96,shards=3] 0.9984; single_node_hnsw[M=32,efConstruction=200,efSearch=128] 0.9976. Their recall differs by less than the calibration tolerance (0.01), which is what this project can currently defend, so choosing between them on recall would be reading noise. They are separated only where they differ measurably. Overall: hash_sharded[M=32,efSearch=96,shards=3] couldnt_check; single_node_hnsw[M=32,efConstruction=200,efSearch=128] meets -- indistinguishable on recall is not indistinguishable overall.

Recommended: single_node_hnsw[M=32,efConstruction=200,efSearch=128]. It meets every constraint that could be checked, and was ranked first by: fewest constraints at margin (3: recall_at_k, latency_p95, qps), then lowest storage amplification (1.00x), then lowest fan-out (1).

single_node_hnsw[M=32,efConstruction=200,efSearch=128] meets latency_p95 in environment tf8sd2usxbblsm: p95 38.22 ms <= 40.0 ms on runpod (environment tf8sd2usxbblsm) (from k=10_under_load: under load at concurrency 32).

rtt_baseline.note: sequential, single client, client-side wall clock. This is a latency shape and is not throughput; nothing here was measured under load.

sequential.outcome: couldnt_check: environment noise -- the baseline RTT p95 (6.99 ms) is 97% of the query p95 (7.18 ms), over the 20% limit, so this measures the path to the engine more than the engine. Recall is unaffected and is reported.

latency.note: latency here is measured UNDER LOAD at the stated concurrency and is a different quantity from the single-client latency shape. Recall is not measured here; it comes from a separate sequential pass so load can never be counted as a recall miss.
